newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil weakens, Russians still well supplied.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil weakens, Russians still well supplied.

text.p: NWE high and low sulphur fuel oil was weaker on Monday as demand sagged and Russian cargoes continued to load in Baltic ports, traders said.
High sulphur barges began the day offered around $98 fob ARA then slipped amid very poor bunker demand. Trade was confirmed as low as $95 but another deal was rumoured done at $93.25.
High sulphur cargoes slipped too. Utility players were seen prepared to pay around $95 cif NWE for product and offers were thought to have moved below $99 cif.
Low sulphur fuel oil was weaker, too, in line with softer crude oil. Physical prices were assessed at $104/$105 fob NWE.
Russian fuel oil exports from the Baltics were assessed at 500-600,000 tonnes in January, compared to 900,000 tonnes in both December and November.
